passage: Two-year-old Aadhya screamed when a pressure cooker whistled beside her, and it took her father Samir a long while to settle her. When the neighbour's drill started up two days later, she clamped her hands over her ears and clung to his neck. He stayed close, swaying with her, and kept the same bedtime song every night. At fifteen, Aadhya swung from anxious about her marks, to snappy at breakfast, to convinced by evening that nobody at school really liked her. Her friend Damini sat on the bench beside her one lunch hour and said only, "You've had a full day of feelings." Aadhya laughed weakly and shared her sandwich. At twenty-five, Aadhya worked at an engineering firm where she reread every report twice. Before a client visit, her worry led her to notice that one figure did not match the drawing, and the problem was fixed before anyone saw it. Damini, now a colleague, looked over. "Good catch." Aadhya nodded, then put her laptop away at six, made tea and sat by the window until her shoulders came down.

qa.q: What did Aadhya's father keep the same every night after the drill?
qa.a: He kept the same bedtime song every night.

qa.q: How does Aadhya's sensitivity look at two, fifteen and twenty-five?
qa.a: At two it showed as hard crying at loud noises until her father settled her, at fifteen as swings between worry, snappiness and self-doubt, and at twenty-five as an alarm that caught a mismatched figure in a report. The same sensitivity became more useful once she also built in rest.

qa.q: What was Aadhya feeling when she was sure that nobody at school really liked her?
qa.a: She felt low and unsure of herself, as her friend Damini could see from a whole day of swinging feelings.

qa.q: What could Aadhya do to keep her careful nature from wearing her out?
qa.a: She could keep closing her laptop at a set time and rest, and treat a worry as information to check rather than a verdict.

grounding: The same person's sensitive temperament appears as a toddler's strong reaction, a teenager's mood swings and self-doubt, and an adult's early risk-spotting that needs rest.
